title: EOS project declaration
description: What this project IS and how it is verified. Authoritative for the product-quality gate (project-gate.mjs), the G-EVAL paradigm signal (eos-doctor.mjs) and the workflow profile (.github/eos/eos.mjs).

language.description: BCP-47 tag for the language agents answer in (e.g. "en", "zh-CN", "ja"). Prose only — code, identifiers, commands and .eos/** records stay English. Unset means: mirror whatever language the developer writes in.

audit.description: Dependency / supply-chain audit (npm audit, pip-audit, cargo audit, govulncheck …). Not part of the per-push quality gate: it is executed by the release gate, where a network failure is DEFERRED and never a PASS.

workflowProfile.description: Key into .eos/workflow.json profiles. Defaults to standard-product.

complianceProfile.description: Advisory declaration only, and it can only TIGHTEN: docs/compliance-profile.json stays the authoritative record of the data-boundary decision (audit EOS-004). Declaring "regulated" here turns the compliance checks on even before that file exists; declaring "none" never turns them off.

evidencePolicy.description: How much provenance this project's release evidence must carry. A regulated project MUST state it — leaving it unset fails, because 'nobody decided' is not a policy. It may legitimately choose "local": an air-gapped environment cannot reach an attestation authority at all, and refusing to ship there would exclude exactly the users who need governance most. State the reason in evidencePolicyReason.

evidencePolicyReason.description: Why this policy is the right one for this project — required when a regulated project chooses "local".

release.description: How releases of this project are bound and signed (eos-2.0.0). `artifacts`: repository-relative paths of what ships; `*` may appear in the file name (dist/*.tgz). `signing.publicKey`: the Ed25519 public key release manifests must be signed with — written by `eos release keygen`.

policyUpstream.description: The organization policy baseline this project follows (ADR-013). `source`: https URL, or file:/path to a checkout of the organization's policy repository. `publicKey`: repository-relative path of the key the baseline must be signed with. `eos policy sync` fetches and vendors it; `eos policy check` enforces it offline.

evidence.description: Where the project's runners write test results EOS turns into gate evidence (eos-2.2.0, ADR-016). `junit`: repository-relative paths or globs (`*`, `**`, `?`) of the JUnit XML reports `commands.test` writes. The `verified` gate reads only the reports that run wrote, answers every docs/trace-matrix.md reference from them and writes docs/evidence/test-run.json itself. Part of the policy lock: changing it is a REVIEW change.

agentPlatforms.description: The agent platforms this team uses (eos-2.2.0, ADR-017; eos-2.3.0, ADR-019), so `eos agents sync` generates what each one reads: the EOS MCP server entry, the guardrail hook in the platform's own format, agents and skill copies where needed. Absent = copilot, claude and antigravity (.agents/, .github/, .claude/ and .mcp.json). kiro, qwen, devin (Windsurf / Devin Desktop), opencode and cline are Tier 2: generated from each vendor's documentation, not yet verified on a real installation. `eos agents sync --platform <x> --write` adds one.

approvalMode.description: Who may approve. `independent` (the default): every approval needs a person other than the one who prepared the work. `solo`: the single maintainer of a Standard-track project may record a labelled self-approval (approve with the self flag and a reason, a policy lock with the self flag, or a waiver approver written `<name> (self)`), recorded as assurance "self" and shown wherever the approval is shown. Never combine with complianceProfile "regulated" or the regulated / controlled profiles (ADR-023).

productTree.description: Records that are not product. `exclude`: exact repository paths (for example docs/pilot-log.md) that stay out of the product-tree digest, so editing them no longer makes every story's evidence STALE. Adding an entry is a policy REVIEW — a second look at what stops being verified.

templateDefault.description: true = this declaration is the EOS template's own (it describes EOS, not your project). A copy of the template inherits it; `eos next` asks for `eos init <pack>` until it is replaced, and `eos init` may replace it without --force.

command.description: A command string, an argv array, or an array of command strings to chain. Null means explicitly not applicable.
